acceptance.invocation: judgment -- recorded, not self-graded. The reads behind it are: aws s3api list-objects-v2 over opal-data-ycharts (38 keys) with every segment run through the constructor's own _check_segment; lambda-source-map.json's file lists for every irpt function; _authz/errors.py's PUBLIC_REASONS and reason_for; and the battery's arm (d) two-sided census
acceptance.output_evidence: (1) WHICH ROUND-1 S3 KEYS ALREADY CARRY A NAME-SHAPED COMPONENT, AND WHAT REMOVING THEM WOULD REQUIRE. MEASURED, not reasoned: every live object in opal-data-ycharts was listed and every segment of every key run through the constructor's OWN new ladder (_check_segment), so the census asks exactly the question the fix asks and cannot drift from it. 38 keys, 251 segments. 6 segments refused, ALL of them NOT_A_DECLARED_SHAPE, and ZERO refused as DISPLAY_NAME_SHAPED or EMAIL_SHAPED. THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION AS ASKED IS: NONE. No key already written carries a name-shaped component. THE SIX ARE WORTH NAMING ANYWAY, because 'refused by the new ladder' and 'carries a name' are different sets and the difference is the whole point. All six are the SAME segment, 'irpt-variants-20260911-comparison', in six sibling keys under research/20260911/variants/synthetic-firm/synthetic-advisor/requests/. It is 33 characters and SEGMENT_WORD_RE admits 32. It is a LENGTH OVERFLOW ON A STRUCTURAL WORD, not a name -- and those six keys are under research/, which is not a declared prefix family at all: they were written by the CRO's variants worker, not by s3_evidence_key. Of the 38 keys, 5 are under firms/ (the declared families this constructor builds) and 33 under research/. ALL FIVE OF THE DECLARED-FAMILY KEYS PASS THE NEW LADDER CLEANLY. WHAT REMOVING THEM WOULD REQUIRE, if the estate ever decided to: nothing, for the reason just given -- there is nothing name-shaped to remove. If the question is instead what removing a name-shaped key WOULD require, the answer is an S3 COPY-THEN-DELETE under a new key plus a rewrite of every reference to the old one, and the references are the hard part: an AnalysisReport row's vendor_artifact and release.protected_pdf_ref both carry a storage_key, the irpt-jobs table carries attempt keys, and a receipt is content-addressed by a key it names. S3 has no rename. That is why the face's bound makes the constructor's refusal FORWARD-ONLY, and on this evidence the bound costs nothing: the forward-only fix is also a complete one. (2) DID THE CLOSED REASON ENUM LOSE A DIAGNOSTIC AN OPERATOR NEEDS? NO -- because the diagnostic MOVED rather than being deleted, and arm (d) measures the move in both directions: 0 occurrences of the injected value in the response, and 18 of 18 correlation ids resolving to an internal record that DOES carry it. That two-sided check is the one that matters. A redaction which destroys the diagnostic is switched off by the first person debugging at 2am, and then the leak returns permanently with a good reason attached. THREE THINGS AN OPERATOR GENUINELY LOST, stated plainly rather than argued away: (i) THE ONE-GLANCE CAUSE. Before, a failure showed 'BadZipFile: File is not a zip file' in the response; now it shows INVALID_INPUT plus corr-<12 hex>, and the cause needs a second lookup. That is a real cost in minutes and it is the price of the property. (ii) RESOLUTION WITHOUT LOG ACCESS. The correlation id is only useful to someone who can read the function's log group. A support person who can see a response but not CloudWatch has strictly less than before. Whether that population exists is a product question I cannot answer from here and am flagging rather than assuming. (iii) THE RESIDUAL CLASS. 14 reasons cover the outcomes the six families reach, but UNEXPECTED is a member of the enum and not an escape hatch -- an unclassified failure still gets a code a consumer can branch on. The risk is that UNEXPECTED quietly becomes the common case, and the only defence I built is that reason_for() maps by TYPE so a new exception class lands in UNEXPECTED visibly. NOBODY COUNTS how often it is returned; a standing count of reason codes by frequency would catch the drift, and building one is a monitor, which bound 2 forbids this project outright. That tension is real and is the CVO's to weigh: the moratorium is correct AND it means this enum's health is unobserved. (3) WHICH ERROR PATH COULD I NOT REACH WITH AN INJECTED EXCEPTION. Four, and they divide into two kinds. NOT REACHED BECAUSE THE CODE IS NOT DEPLOYED ANYWHERE (the sharper kind): intake/parse.py and intake/corrections.py are in NO function's packaged file list in lambda-source-map.json. Three of the ten paths this cell fixed live in them -- including the jsonschema ValidationError path, which was the worst of the ten because a ValidationError's first line quotes the INSTANCE, so a holdings row carrying a client name went into a contract-validation report. They are fixed in the repo, exercised by the local suite, and serve nothing today. An injected exception reaches them in-process and can never reach them in a deployed function, because there is no deployed function containing them. NOT REACHED BECAUSE THE PATH IS DEAD ON IMPORT: export/download.py's error paths. Its module-level `import enforce` fails in the deployed zip (row W3-S14), so nothing in that file executes in AWS at all. NOT REACHED BECAUSE THE DEPENDENCY WILL NOT FAIL ON DEMAND: the two paths that catch an ImportError for jsonschema (export/bundle.py) and for pdfplumber (ycharts/extract). I can force them by manipulating sys.modules, which is a self-wrapping harness and bound 12 forbids it as evidence; in the deployed function they fire only when a layer is genuinely absent. Their fix is the trivial one (render the exception's TYPE, not the exception), and they are asserted by reading rather than by execution. AND ONE CATEGORY THE QUESTION DOES NOT ASK ABOUT BUT THAT BOUNDS THE ANSWER: arm (c)'s census reads EXCEPT HANDLERS, so a public reason built on an ORDINARY RETURN is outside its denominator entirely. One such path existed -- directory/handler.py returned 'ERROR: unsupported op ' + repr(op), reflecting caller input -- and it surfaced only because a directory test failed against a neighbouring change. '0 of 49 except handlers render the exception' is true and is NOT the same claim as 'no public reason carries caller data'. Row IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S15.

mutant.description: The arms carry their own discriminators rather than a separate mutant file, and for this cell that is stronger: every arm was OBSERVED FAILING on the real artifact before it passed, which is a mutation of the subject rather than of a copy. Arm (a) was run against the module AT ROUND-1 HEAD and reported 6 of 24 pairs ACCEPTED -- that is the pre-fix state of the very code being graded. Arm (c)'s census reported 10 handlers rendering the exception before the edits and 0 after, over the same real modules. Two further negative controls are built in: error_envelope() is called with a reason outside the enum and must raise (printed 'a free-string reason is refused: True'), and the import-closure check is run against a zip that is genuinely incomplete.
mutant.expected: Each arm must be capable of reading FAIL on the real artifact, and must have been seen doing so rather than assumed to. A free-string public reason must raise. An incomplete zip must report OPEN.
mutant.observed: ALL OBSERVED. Round-1 HEAD, 7 constructors x 4 negatives: s3_evidence_key ACCEPTED 'Whitfield Family' and 'AAMkAGI2THVSAAA='; quarantine_key ACCEPTED all four. After the fix, 27 refused with 0 leaks and 1 positional admission. The error-path census: 10 rendering before, 0 after. error_envelope('MADE_UP_REASON') raises ReasonNotDeclared -> 'a free-string reason is refused: True'. The import-closure check reports 'irpt-export-render ... import 6 of 7 OPEN / IMPORT FAILED download ModuleNotFoundError: No module named enforce'. And arm (e) reads FAIL at rc 1 with the token withheld. TWO DEFECTS WERE FOUND IN THIS CELL'S OWN INSTRUMENTS, both by two instruments disagreeing, and both are recorded because they are the more instructive half: (i) THE BATTERY REPORTED A CLEANER IMPORT CLOSURE THAN THE TRUTH -- 6 of 6 in-process against the standalone script's 5 of 6, because the battery imports modules of its own first and a packaged module's `import enforce` resolved from a leftover sys.modules entry. The check whose entire purpose is to prove a zip stands alone was leaning on the process it ran in. A saved-and-restored sys.modules is not isolation; only a new interpreter is. It now runs in a clean subprocess and reports 5 of 6. (ii) THE ERROR-PATH CENSUS OVER-FIRED 2 OF 12 by counting type(exc).__name__ as a rendering; the two false positives were modules that had already applied this lesson deliberately, one of them citing row W2-S10 in a comment. A census that over-fires sends a careful reader to 'fix' correct code AND inflates the denominator its own fix is graded against, so '10 of 10 closed' would have read as '12 of 12'.

declared_exclusions.reason: Bounds 1 and 2. This cell makes no vendor call of any kind; its only live reads are AWS control-plane and S3 reads against Opal's own account.

surprises: IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S13: the ruling named one leaky key constructor and the census found two. Measured at round-1 HEAD, 6 of 24 (constructor, negative) pairs were ACCEPTED: s3_evidence_key took a display name and a raw upstream key, and quarantine_key took ALL FOUR including an e-mail address. Quarantine is the worse one to have left open, because a message is written there precisely when its origin could NOT be verified. Both are fixed and the twelve round-1 keys still build byte-identically. The point of the row is the method: verifying only the constructor the ruling named would have left quarantine_key untouched and recorded W3-S12 as closed.

IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S14: the deployed export download route is dead on import. export/download.py does `import enforce` at module level and enforce.py has never been in irpt-export-render's packaged file list; handler.py imports download lazily, so the function cold-starts fine and fails only when the route is first exercised. Found by an import-closure check, which exists because CodeSha256 equality proves the bytes served are the bytes built and says nothing about whether they can be imported.

IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S15: arm (c)'s denominator is except handlers, and a public reason can be built without one. directory/handler.py returned 'ERROR: unsupported op ' + repr(op) on an ordinary return, reflecting caller input into a public reason where no AST census of except handlers could see it. It surfaced only because a directory test failed against a neighbouring change. '0 of 49 except handlers render the exception' is true and is not the same claim as 'no public reason carries caller data'.

IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S16: the ruling says twelve %r message sites become zero; the module carried eighteen placeholders across sixteen construction sites when this cell measured it. All eighteen are now zero, so the fix satisfies either reading -- but a later reader checking 'did twelve become zero' against a file that had eighteen cannot tell whether six were missed or six never existed. A count is a measurement with a vintage and this one carries none.

IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S17 (BLOCKING): the export Terraform root cannot be applied without destroying three live resources this ruling did not order. aws_iam_role_policy.export_render_dispatch, aws_iam_role_policy.export_render_evidence and aws_ssm_document.export_render_run are in state and not in configuration, left by IB-s-14 at 1beda4bf49 without an apply, so the plan reads '0 to add, 1 to change, 3 to destroy' before any change of this cell's. irpt-export-render's code is committed and its apply is withheld; RT4-AC1 arm (e) fails and this order stays open. A second writer is also on that root -- its served CodeSha256 moved during this cell's run.

IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S18: the source map's registered hash for irpt-export-render agrees with neither S3 nor the live function, while those two agree with each other -- so the registry the estate's CodeSha256 checks compare against is the one that is wrong. The dangerous direction: a later reader sees MISMATCH on a correctly-deployed function and the obvious remedy pushes stale bytes over a healthy one. This cell deliberately did not register a hash for a function it is not deploying.

compiler_tools.result: ENUMERATE-END: 4 hit(s) | 4 whole | 0 sub | DEF=1 CODE=2 COMMENT=1, scanned 1 of 1. Located the single raise site and the single catch site before changing either, which is how the catch was found to be reading an already-sanitized message -- safe at that site and unsafe in principle at any other, since the class is public.

Resolved two source-map members that do not live in their function's source_dir (irpt-status packages directory/handler.py and intake/checkpoint.py flat). Without that the zip builder reported BUILD FAILED on irpt-status and the import-closure check could not have run at all.

compiler_tools.tool: comp-iam service (Phase 1, per the order's preflight)
compiler_tools.invocation: comp-iam service <each function whose code changes>
compiler_tools.result: DECLARED-NOT-EXERCISED for this cell and stated as such: no policy, role or trust document is written or changed by IB-rt-4 -- every pre-apply plan shows s3_object_version and source_code_hash as the only differing attributes, and 0 to add / 0 to destroy on all four applied roots. The IAM surface this cell DID touch is the one it refused to touch: the export root's plan would have DESTROYED two aws_iam_role_policy resources, which is row W3-S17 and the reason arm (e) fails.

compiler_tools.tool: comp-iam gaps (Phase 2, per the order's preflight)
compiler_tools.result: Carried from the round-1 cut as the preflight allows (191 roles parsed, 307 gaps estate-wide) and NOT re-run, because this cell adds and removes no grant. Recorded with the preflight's own disclosed blind spot: DESIRED plane only, and a GRANTED-BROAD wildcard cannot be falsified by a resource check.

compiler_tools.invocation: deploy_ledger.py open --slug irpt-bckend-rt4-{directory,intake,ycharts,ops} (5 legs each) ... close-leg L1..L5 ... close
compiler_tools.result: 'OK: CLOSED ... all 5 legs proven; sentinel removed' on all four. All four sentinels were committed OPEN in ONE commit (48313e9c0e) before any upload or apply and removed in ONE commit (a36c28a079) before the grading reads -- the ordering row W3-S4 asks for, at two commits instead of ten. No entry was opened for export, because no act was taken there.

directory '0 added, 2 changed, 0 destroyed'; intake, ycharts and ops '0 added, 1 changed, 0 destroyed' each. Every root was `init`-ed first with the vendored binary, because provider caches were purged estate-wide. Never a bare terraform apply and never a PATH terraform.

compiler_tools.tool: an import-closure check in a clean subprocess (the instrument that found two defects)
compiler_tools.invocation: extract each built zip to a temp directory and import every packaged module with the WORKTREE EXCLUDED from sys.path -- the /var/task layout
compiler_tools.result: 5 of 6 CLOSED. It found row W3-S14 (export/download.py needs a module its zip has never contained) and it found a FALSE GREEN in this cell's own battery, which ran the same check in-process and reported 6 of 6 because a leftover sys.modules entry satisfied the import. Run BEFORE each hash was registered, not after, because a CodeSha256 match on a function that dies at import passes every other rung.

compiler_tools.tool: aws s3api list-objects-v2 + the constructor's own _check_segment (RT4-AC2 Q1)
compiler_tools.invocation: list every key in opal-data-ycharts and run every segment of every key through keys._check_segment
compiler_tools.result: 38 keys, 251 segments, 6 refused -- ALL NOT_A_DECLARED_SHAPE, ZERO DISPLAY_NAME_SHAPED or EMAIL_SHAPED. The 6 are one 33-character structural word against a 32-character limit, in six sibling keys under research/, which is not a declared prefix family. All 5 keys under firms/ pass cleanly. The test is the constructor's OWN ladder, so the census cannot drift from the fix it is measuring.

Clean on every file. It caught real defects rather than rubber-stamping: an undefined-name on a first wiring attempt that would have broken directory/handler.py at import, plus three unused imports and variables in the battery.
